column_order: every dataset lists its variables in an order drawn from its seed, with the true graph permuted the same way
error_metric: each comparison row's own: median shd of the learned graph against the true graph's CPDAG (mec_shd for a DAG, the PAG for FCI)

speed.cores_per_fit: 1 for the one-worker rows (a fit on one thread, pinned to two CPUs of a 4-CPU slot, the second for the harness), 4 for the four-worker rows and the Tetrad rows
speed.fits: speed rows: one unit per row on one node and one CPU model (a 4-CPU slot of a shared node), both builds in the same job; each dataset is fit by one build and then the other, the order swapped on alternate rounds, each fit in its own process after 0 or 1 untimed warm-up fit (the row's warmup); a 1800 s wall cap and a 20000 MB memory cap per fit. Comparison rows: one job per group on one node, both packages on the same datasets; GES against pcalg on one core, 3 timed repeats per dataset after 1 warm-up fit each, a 1800 s wall cap and a 20000 MB cap; the Tetrad lanes on 4 cores, one timed fit after 1 warm-up (Tetrad's in the same JVM), a 1800 s wall cap and a 30000 MB cap

not_generated.reason: not generated: the temporal data generator found no stationary VAR draw for d=240 in 1,000 tries, so no build was timed; not a timeout

builds.older: andrey-core 0.8.0 from PyPI, the same dependency versions as the current build's environment

speed.note: Andrey 0.9.0 against Andrey 0.8.0 on the same datasets, the same parameters, and the same cores, in one job on one node per size. A dataset's time is the median over its rounds; seconds_080 and seconds_090 are medians over the size's datasets, and speedup is their ratio, with the per-dataset extremes in speedup_min and speedup_max. same_output holds when every fit of both builds returned the same output.
speed.comparisons_note: Andrey 0.9.0 against another package on the same datasets, on the same node in one job. A dataset's time is the median over its repeats; seconds_ref and seconds_090 are medians over the size's datasets, and speedup is seconds_ref / seconds_090. errors_ref and errors_090 are each side's median shd against the true graph's CPDAG (mec_shd for a DAG; the PAG of the observed variables for FCI). same_graph_datasets counts the datasets on which both packages returned the same graph. For Tetrad, seconds_ref is the search inside the JVM (JVM start, source compile, and data loading excluded, as Andrey's time excludes interpreter start and imports) and process_s_ref is the whole call. A fit that did not finish never scores: its dataset leaves the medians and stop_ref or stop_090 says why. The comparisons with Tetrad are under review and are published with 0.10.0.
